requirements.quote: write native Python Playwright scripts for testing local web applications

requirements.reason: The --help run comes before using with_server.py. The always rule also says to start with --help.

requirements.quote: read a bundled script's source unless running it with --help was tried and a customized solution is absolutely necessary
requirements.reason: Same prohibition with the same condition. The source read is gated on this condition in the flow.

requirements.quote: run bundled scripts directly as black boxes, starting with --help
requirements.reason: Black-box use is required. The built skill does not say to consider a bundled script before writing custom code. Only with_server.py is used in the flow, and only when the server is not running.

requirements.quote:
verify #html-complete html is complete enough to identify selectors from html
      otherwise:
        return to dynamic
requirements.reason: Static HTML is read directly. A read failure or incomplete HTML falls back to the dynamic path.

requirements.quote: exec #servers with_server.py with one --server and --port pair per server, then the automation script from with_server as result
requirements.reason: When the server is not running, the --help run comes first and with_server.py then manages the servers.

requirements.quote: inspect the DOM before waiting for networkidle on dynamic apps
requirements.reason: The prohibition is scoped to dynamic apps. The static path has no wait, as the source allows.
The order is inspect, then identify selectors, then act. This is enforced for the running-server path.

requirements.quote: keep the automation script to Playwright logic only when with_server.py manages the servers
launch chromium headless with sync_playwright and p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
close the browser when automation is done
launch chromium headless with sync_playwright and p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
Use descriptive selectors (`text=`, `role=`, CSS selectors, or IDs). Add appropriate waits with `page.wait_for_selector()` or `page.wait_for_timeout()`. Use judgment on both.
requirements.reason: This sits in a Taste section, and 'Use judgment on both' turns the source's best-practice obligation into a soft preference. It is not in the contract.
